mainTopic: Removing פרה and עגלה ערופה from רבי שמעון's list, two buyers of a cow and its calf, and counting lashes for אותו ואת בנו
overview: The amud begins by testing two cases in רבי שמעון's list of 'unfit' slaughters, the פרת חטאת and the עגלה ערופה. Slaughtering either of these may still be a fit slaughter, so רבי שמעון might hold the slaughterer liable for אותו ואת בנו. For both cases the answer is that the case 'is not part of the משנה.' The גמרא then argues about who said this about the עגלה ערופה. רבי ינאי could not have said it, since he could have split the case into before and after the heifer's descent to the נחל איתן. ריש לקיש could not have said it either, because he learns the מצורע's birds from the עגלה ערופה and so holds it is forbidden while alive. So the statement is given to רבי יוחנן. A new משנה then rules that when two people bought a cow and its calf, the first buyer slaughters first, though this is only a court matter. Whoever goes first is 'זריז ונשכר.' Another משנה counts lashes by forbidden acts, and סומכוס disagrees about the middle generation slaughtered last. Finally, a ברייתא learns from the plural לא תשחטו that the איסור covers both orders, mother then offspring and offspring then mother.

steps.title: A red heifer can be redeemed even on its pyre
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש reports that רבי שמעון holds a פרה can be redeemed even after it is placed on its pyre. This makes it hard to call its slaughter 'unfit.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש said: רבי שמעון used to say that a red heifer can be redeemed even when it is already on its pyre.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is challenging why רבי שמעון exempts someone who slaughters a פרת חטאת. It brings ריש לקיש's report that, for רבי שמעון, the פרה can still be redeemed even after slaughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון only exempts from אותו ואת בנו when the slaughter could never make the animal permitted. But if the פרה can be redeemed even on its pyre, it could become permitted, so its slaughter looks like a שחיטה ראויה. That seems to contradict listing it in our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The red heifer (פרה אדומה), also called פרת חטאת
Can be redeemed (exchanged for money, removing its holiness)
Upon its pyre, already arranged for burning

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
Rabbi Shimon used to say,
the heifer can be redeemed upon its pyre.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: אוֹמֵר הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the challenge against the פרה case in the משנה (the question itself comes just before this part of the text)
steps.kashyaTarget: The inclusion of פרת חטאת among רבי שמעון's exempt cases in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since רבי שמעון holds the פרה is redeemable even on its pyre, its slaughter can lead to permission, so it is a שחיטה ראויה and he should hold the slaughterer liable.

steps.title: The red heifer is not part of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the פרת חטאת case should not be in the משנה's list of exemptions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמן בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the פרת חטאת is not part of the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by removing the פרה case from the משנה. רבי שמעון actually agrees that someone who slaughters it is liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of explaining why the פרה's slaughter is 'unfit,' רבי יוחנן accepts the challenge. The פרה really is a fit slaughter for רבי שמעון, so it does not belong in his list of exemptions.

keyTerms.meaning: The red heifer whose ashes are used for purification
It is not part of the משנה, meaning it should be removed from the list

phrases.english: Rav Shemen bar Abba said
Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The heifer of purification is not part of the mishna.
phrases.notes: He means: take this case off the משנה's list of cases where רבי שמעון exempts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removing a case from the משנה's text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: פרה is one of the cases where רבי שמעון exempts
steps.terutzMaskana: פרה is not in the משנה; רבי שמעון holds its slaughterer liable for אותו ואת בנו

steps.title: The neck-broken heifer can go back to graze
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the עגלה ערופה case. A משנה says that if the murderer is found before the neck is broken, the heifer goes back to graze, so it is not forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And isn't the עגלה ערופה a fit slaughter? But we learned in a משנה: if the murderer was found before the heifer's neck was broken, it goes out and grazes with the flock.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the same kind of question about the עגלה ערופה case in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the neck is broken, the עגלה is not forbidden. If the murderer turns up, it simply goes back to the herd. So if someone slaughters it before that point, the slaughter could make it permitted, which makes it a שחיטה ראויה.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'fit' slaughter, one that can make the animal permitted
The murderer was found
Will have its neck broken
Will graze among the flock, as an ordinary permitted animal

phrases.aramaic: וְעֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה, לָאו שְׁחִיטָה רְאוּיָה הִיא?
phrases.english: And the heifer whose neck is to be broken, is it not a fit slaughter?
But didn't we learn in a mishna:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in סוטה 47a.

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצָא הַהוֹרֵג עַד שֶׁלֹּא תֵּעָרֵף הָעֲגָלָה –
phrases.english: If the murderer was found before the heifer's neck was broken,
it goes out and grazes among the flock.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה, לָאו שְׁחִיטָה רְאוּיָה הִיא? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same kind of challenge to the next case in the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The inclusion of עגלה ערופה among רבי שמעון's exempt cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The עגלה is permitted before its neck is broken, so slaughtering it then is a שחיטה ראויה, and רבי שמעון should hold the slaughterer liable.

steps.title: The neck-broken heifer is not part of the משנה either
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, in the name of רבי ינאי, answers that the עגלה ערופה case also does not belong in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said in the name of רבי ינאי: the עגלה ערופה is not part of the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same kind of answer as before. It removes the עגלה ערופה from the משנה's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ינאי accepts that slaughtering the עגלה is a fit slaughter. So רבי שמעון agrees the slaughterer is liable, and the case is taken off the list.

keyTerms.meaning: The heifer whose neck is broken to atone for an unsolved murder
Here: the list of cases written in our משנה

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said in the name of Rabbi Yannai:
The heifer whose neck is broken is not part of the mishna.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removing a case from the משנה's text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עגלה ערופה is one of the cases where רבי שמעון exempts
steps.terutzMaskana: עגלה ערופה is not in the משנה; רבי שמעון holds its slaughterer liable

steps.title: Rabbi Yannai said the heifer's descent makes it forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי ינאי really said this. Elsewhere he reports a point after which the עגלה becomes forbidden: its going down to the נחל איתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי ינאי really say that? But רבי ינאי said: I heard of a point where it becomes forbidden, but I forgot it, and the group of scholars leaned toward saying that its going down to the hard valley makes it forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 4 by quoting another statement of רבי ינאי himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ינאי's second statement shows that, for him, there is a stage before the neck-breaking when the עגלה already becomes forbidden: its descent to the valley. After that point, slaughtering it would be an 'unfit' slaughter. The next step spells out why this is a problem for his first statement.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Did he really say so?', which introduces a contradiction from the same sage
A boundary, the stage after which it becomes forbidden
The group of scholars leaned toward (saying)
The hard (rough) valley where the neck is broken
Makes it forbidden

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yannai say so?
But didn't Rabbi Yannai say:
I heard a boundary regarding it, but I forgot,
phrases.notes: He heard there is a specific stage when the עגלה becomes forbidden, but he forgot which stage it was.

phrases.english: and the group of scholars were inclined to say:
its descent to a hard valley renders it forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 4 using another statement by the same sage
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי's answer that עגלה ערופה is not part of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי ינאי holds there is a stage (the descent) after which the עגלה is forbidden, so he had a way to keep it in the משנה as an unfit slaughter.

steps.title: He could have answered: before descent versus after descent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sharpens the challenge. If רבי ינאי held of the descent rule, he should have kept the משנה by saying it speaks about slaughter after the descent.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if that is so, let him answer: here it is before the descent, and there it is after the descent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge by showing the easier answer רבי ינאי should have given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in סוטה (the עגלה goes back to graze) would be talking about before the descent, when the עגלה is still permitted. Our משנה (רבי שמעון exempts) would be talking about slaughter after the descent, when the עגלה is already forbidden. Since רבי ינאי holds of the descent rule, the גמרא doubts that he is really the one who said 'עגלה ערופה is not part of the משנה.' The next step answers by giving that statement to someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it is so
Let him answer (resolve the contradiction)
Before the descent to the valley
After the descent to the valley

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two sources. 'Before the descent' explains the משנה in סוטה, where the עגלה is still permitted and goes back to graze. 'After the descent' explains our משנה, where the slaughter is unfit, so רבי שמעון exempts.
steps.whatToRemember: Both פרה and עגלה ערופה were removed from רבי שמעון's list, because their slaughter can still be fit. But the second removal is now in question, since רבי ינאי could have kept the עגלה by splitting before and after its descent.

phrases.english: And if it is so, let him resolve it:
Here it is before the descent,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the משנה in סוטה, where the עגלה goes back to graze; 'there' is our משנה, where רבי שמעון exempts.

phrases.english: there it is after the descent.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אִיתָא, לִישַׁנֵּי: כָּאן קוֹדֶם יְרִידָה, כָּאן לְאַחַר יְרִידָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge of step 5 by showing the alternative answer רבי ינאי should have given
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי's choice to remove עגלה ערופה from the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Holding that the descent makes the עגלה forbidden would let him split the two משניות (before descent and after descent), so there was no need to remove the case from the משנה.

steps.title: The statement was taught in ריש לקיש's own name
steps.stepSummary: רב פנחס says the line 'עגלה ערופה is not part of the משנה' was taught in ריש לקיש's own name, not as a quote from רבי ינאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פנחס בריה דרב אמי said: We learned this statement in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש himself: the עגלה ערופה does not belong in the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from steps 5-6 by changing who said the statement. It was ריש לקיש speaking for himself, not quoting רבי ינאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that רבי ינאי holds the עגלה is forbidden once it goes down to the נחל איתן, so he could have kept the משנה. If רבי ינאי never said this statement, that problem goes away. Now the statement belongs only to ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: We teach it / we learned it (this is the version we have)
It is not part of the משנה; the case should be removed from the list
The heifer whose neck is broken when a murdered body is found and the killer is unknown

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פִּנְחָס בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rav Pinchas son of Rav Ami said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנַן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
phrases.english: We, in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish,
phrases.notes: He means רבי שמעון בן לקיש said it on his own, without quoting רבי ינאי.

phrases.english: teach it:
the heifer whose neck is broken is not part of the mishna.

steps.triggerLanguage: אנן משמיה דרבי שמעון בן לקיש מתנינן לה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from steps 5-6 by removing רבי ינאי from the chain of attribution.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Change of attribution: the statement belongs to ריש לקיש alone, not רבי ינאי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought ריש לקיש was quoting רבי ינאי, who holds the עגלה is forbidden after going down to the נחל איתן.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי ינאי never said it, so his ruling about the descent does not contradict it.

steps.title: רב אשי doubts that ריש לקיש said it
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports that in רב פפי's study hall they asked: did ריש לקיש really say this?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: When we were in רב פפי's study hall, we had a difficulty: did רבי שמעון בן לקיש really say this?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי questions the new attribution from step 7. This line sets up the challenge, and the proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving the statement to ריש לקיש solved the רבי ינאי problem. But רב אשי suspects that ריש לקיש's own known views contradict it, and he is about to show why.

keyTerms.meaning: It was difficult for us; we had a problem with it
The study hall of a teacher
Did he really say...? (a doubting question)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
When we were in the study hall of Rav Pappi
it was difficult for us:

phrases.aramaic: מִי אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ הָכִי?
phrases.english: Did Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish really say this?

steps.triggerLanguage: קשיא לן מי אמר רבי שמעון בן לקיש הכי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the attribution just given in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ריש לקיש said 'עגלה ערופה is not part of the משנה'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ריש לקיש's own known views may contradict this statement, which the next step will show.

steps.title: The dispute over when the leper's birds become forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי brings a dispute: רבי יוחנן says the צפורי מצורע are forbidden from slaughter, and ריש לקיש says from the time they are taken. The גמרא asks for ריש לקיש's reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was stated: from when are the צפורי מצורע forbidden? רבי יוחנן says: from the time of slaughter. רבי שמעון בן לקיש says: from the time they are taken. And we asked: what is רבי שמעון בן לקיש's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings a source to back up his doubt. It is a dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about the birds a מצורע brings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש holds the birds are forbidden from the moment they are taken, while still alive. The question 'what is his reason?' sets up the key point. His reason will tie the birds to the עגלה ערופה.

keyTerms.meaning: The two birds a מצורע brings for his purification
Become forbidden (to get any benefit from)
From the time of slaughter
From the time they are taken (chosen for the מצוה)

phrases.english: But it was stated:
The birds of a metzora, from when are they forbidden?
Rabbi Yochanan says: from the time of slaughter,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: מִשְּׁעַת לְקִיחָה,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says: from the time they are taken,
and we said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ?
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish?

steps.triggerLanguage: והא איתמר צפורי מצורע מאימתי נאסרין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind רב אשי's doubt in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The attribution to ריש לקיש from step 7.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ריש לקיש's view on the מצורע's birds depends on how he views the עגלה ערופה, which the next step reveals.

steps.title: ריש לקיש learns the birds from the heifer
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש's reason is a גזרה שוה: the word 'taking' appears by the birds and by the עגלה ערופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns 'taking' from 'taking' of the heifer whose neck is broken.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 9. ריש לקיש learns the birds' rule from the עגלה ערופה because the תורה says 'take' by both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the birds are forbidden from taking because of the עגלה ערופה, then the עגלה itself must be forbidden from its taking, while still alive. So for ריש לקיש its slaughter does not make it fit to eat, and the משנה's case works perfectly. He would have no reason to say it is not part of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns (one case from another)
'Taking', the shared word that links the two cases
Learning a law from one case to another through a shared word in the תורה

steps.confusionAlert: This line looks like it only explains the birds, but its real job is to show that ריש לקיש holds the עגלה ערופה is forbidden while alive. That is what makes it impossible for him to remove the case from the משנה.

phrases.english: He learns "taking" from "taking"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:4 says 'take' about the birds, and דברים 21:3 says 'take' about the heifer.

phrases.english: from the heifer whose neck is broken.

steps.triggerLanguage: גמר קיחה קיחה מעגלה ערופה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question at the end of step 9, and so completes רב אשי's challenge.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does ריש לקיש hold the מצורע's birds are forbidden from the time they are taken?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He learns it through a גזרה שוה of 'taking' from the עגלה ערופה, which shows that the עגלה is forbidden from its taking.

steps.title: The statement really belongs to רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי חייא בר אבא quoted רבי יוחנן as saying the עגלה ערופה case is not part of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי חייא בר אבא said that רבי יוחנן said: the עגלה ערופה does not belong in the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: Since ריש לקיש cannot be the author, the גמרא gives the statement to רבי יוחנן instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן holds the birds are forbidden only from slaughter, so he does not learn from the עגלה ערופה's 'taking'. He can therefore hold that the עגלה is not forbidden while alive, which fits the משנה that says it goes back to graze. So the עגלה ערופה case does not belong in the משנה's list.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; drop the earlier version and take this one

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, רבי יוחנן is the one who removes both the פרת חטאת case and the עגלה ערופה case from the משנה. ריש לקיש could not say this, because he holds the עגלה ערופה is forbidden from the moment it is taken.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
the heifer whose neck is broken is not part of the mishna.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא אמר רבי חייא בר אבא אמר רבי יוחנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts רב אשי's challenge and moves the statement from ריש לקיש to רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Change of attribution: the statement belongs to רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The statement was ריש לקיש's, either on his own or quoting רבי ינאי.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is רבי יוחנן's, which fits his view that the מצורע's birds are forbidden only from slaughter.

steps.title: Two buyers of a cow and its calf
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that the first buyer slaughters first, but if the second buyer slaughters first, he has won.
steps.simpleTranslation: If two people bought a cow and its offspring, whoever bought first slaughters first. If the second one went ahead first, he gained.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts a new topic. Two people each bought one animal, a mother and its offspring, and only one of them may slaughter today.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the mother and its offspring may not be slaughtered on the same day, one buyer has to wait until tomorrow. The משנה gives priority to whoever bought first. Still, if the second buyer slaughters first, the result stands and he is the one who gets to eat today.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
A cow and its offspring
Went first, got there before the other
He gained / he won the right

phrases.english: MISHNA: Two people who bought a cow and its offspring,
whoever bought first should slaughter first,
and if the second one went ahead first, he gained.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שְׁנַיִם שֶׁלָּקְחוּ פָּרָה וּבְנָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the earlier discussion of עגלה ערופה and צפורי מצורע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first buyer has priority to slaughter. If the second buyer slaughters first, he keeps the gain.

steps.title: The priority only matters in court
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that the משנה's priority for the first buyer is about a court ruling, not a prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: We learned this regarding a court judgment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what kind of rule 'the first buyer slaughters first' is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think the second buyer does something forbidden if he slaughters first. רב יוסף says no. The rule only tells a בית דין what to decide if the two buyers come to argue. Without a court case, there is no איסור in going first.

keyTerms.meaning: Regarding a court judgment, meaning if they come to בית דין

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Yosef said:
We learned this regarding a court judgment,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: לְעִנְיַן דִּינָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how far the משנה's priority rule reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first buyer's priority is a court ruling, not a prohibition on the second buyer.

steps.title: A ברייתא praises the one who went first
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the second buyer who slaughtered first is diligent and rewarded. This supports רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: If the second one went first, he is diligent and rewarded. Diligent, because he did not do anything forbidden. Rewarded, because he gets to eat meat today.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רב יוסף's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If going first were forbidden, the ברייתא would not praise the second buyer. It calls him זריז because he did no איסור, since only the one who slaughters later breaks the rule. It calls him נשכר because he gets meat today. This shows the priority is not a prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: Diligent and rewarded, meaning his speed paid off
A forbidden act
Meat

steps.whatToRemember: Who slaughters first between two buyers is only a question for court. The one who goes first does nothing wrong and even gains.

phrases.english: It was taught: If the second one went first,
he is diligent and rewarded;
diligent, because he did not do anything forbidden,
and rewarded, because he gets to eat meat.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנָא: אִם קָדַם הַשֵּׁנִי – הֲרֵי זֶה זָרִיז וְנִשְׂכָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יוסף's statement with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that the first buyer's priority is only a court matter.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that calls the second buyer who went first 'זריז ונשכר'.

steps.title: Counting lashes for several animals
steps.stepSummary: The משנה counts lashes: one set for each separate slaughter that breaks the איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slaughtered a cow and then its two offspring, he gets eighty lashes. If he slaughtered the two offspring and then the cow, he gets forty. If he slaughtered the cow, its daughter, and its daughter's daughter, he gets eighty.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה explains how many sets of lashes someone gets when he slaughters several related animals on one day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lashes are counted by forbidden acts. Mother first, then two offspring: each offspring is a separate forbidden act, so there are two sets (eighty). Two offspring first, then the mother: only the last act is forbidden, so there is one set (forty). Mother, daughter, granddaughter in order: the daughter breaks the איסור because of her mother, and the granddaughter breaks it because of her mother. That makes two acts, so eighty.

keyTerms.meaning: Receives (lashes)
Eighty, meaning two sets of lashes
Forty, meaning one set of lashes
Her daughter's daughter

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ שָׁחַט פָּרָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ שְׁנֵי בָּנֶיהָ –
phrases.english: MISHNA: If he slaughtered a cow and afterward its two offspring,
he receives eighty lashes,

phrases.aramaic: שָׁחַט שְׁנֵי בָּנֶיהָ וְאַחַר כָּךְ שְׁחָטָהּ –
phrases.english: if he slaughtered its two offspring and afterward slaughtered it,
he receives the forty lashes,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁחָטָהּ וְאֶת בִּתָּהּ וְאֶת בַּת בִּתָּהּ –
phrases.english: if he slaughtered it, and its daughter, and its daughter's daughter,
he receives eighty lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שָׁחַט פָּרָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ שְׁנֵי בָּנֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה moving from who slaughters first to how lashes are counted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each separate slaughter that breaks אותו ואת בנו gets its own set of lashes.

steps.title: Middle generation slaughtered last
steps.stepSummary: If the grandmother and granddaughter were slaughtered first and the daughter last, the תנא קמא gives only one set of lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slaughtered the cow and its daughter's daughter, and afterward slaughtered its daughter, he receives forty lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a harder case: the middle animal, which is linked to both of the others, is slaughtered last.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The grandmother and granddaughter are not mother and offspring, so slaughtering them is fine. Only the last act, slaughtering the daughter, is forbidden. Even though that one act connects her to her mother and to her own daughter, it is still one act, so he gets one set (forty).

keyTerms.meaning: Her daughter, the middle generation

steps.confusionAlert: Don't count by how many animals are related. Count by how many slaughtering acts were forbidden. Here only one act was forbidden.

phrases.english: If he slaughtered it and its daughter's daughter,
and afterward slaughtered its daughter,
he receives the forty lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁחָטָהּ וְאֶת בַּת בִּתָּהּ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ שָׁחַט בִּתָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list with a case where one act connects to two relatives.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One forbidden act gets one set of lashes, even if it connects to two related animals.

steps.title: סומכוס disagrees: eighty lashes
steps.stepSummary: סומכוס, quoting רבי מאיר, says the last case gets eighty lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: סומכוס says in the name of רבי מאיר: He receives eighty lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה records a disagreement about the last case. סומכוס holds there are two sets of lashes there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For סומכוס, slaughtering the daughter breaks the איסור twice at once: once as the offspring of her mother, and once as the mother of her own daughter. So one act can earn two sets of lashes. The תנא קמא counts by acts, so he gives only forty.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא counts lashes by acts. סומכוס, in the name of רבי מאיר, counts how many איסורים one act breaks.

phrases.english: Sumakhos says in the name of Rabbi Meir:
He receives eighty lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹמְכוֹס אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר: סוֹפֵג שְׁמוֹנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא's ruling in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One slaughter that breaks the איסור in two directions gets two sets of lashes.

steps.title: Why lashes when the mother is slaughtered last?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: the פסוק says 'it and its offspring,' meaning mother first, so why is someone punished for slaughtering the offspring first and the mother after?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Why? The תורה said 'it and its offspring,' not 'its offspring and it'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by questioning the משנה. If the mother is slaughtered after her offspring, why should there be lashes at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words of the פסוק, אותו ואת בנו, put the mother ('it') first and the offspring second. Read literally, this suggests the איסור only covers slaughtering the mother and then the child. The משנה punishes the reverse order too, so the גמרא wants to know the source.

keyTerms.meaning: Why? (a question asking for the reason)
'The Merciful One', a name for ה׳ as the One who gave the Torah
'It and its offspring', the איסור against slaughtering a mother animal and its young on the same day

steps.confusionAlert: 'אותו' here means the mother animal, and 'בנו' means its offspring. 'בנו ואותו' is the reverse order: offspring first, then the mother.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Why?
phrases.notes: He is asking about the משנה's case where the mother is slaughtered last. Why should that bring lashes?

phrases.english: The Merciful One said 'it and its offspring,'
and not 'its offspring and it'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי? ״אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא now begins analyzing the משנה, starting with the case where the mother is slaughtered after her offspring.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that slaughtering the offspring first and the mother afterward brings lashes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק lists the mother first ('it and its offspring'), which suggests only that order is forbidden.

steps.title: Do not think so: a ברייתא raises the same question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that order matters. It brings a ברייתא that itself notices the פסוק only mentions mother-then-offspring and asks where the reverse order comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not think that, as a ברייתא teaches: From 'it and its offspring' I only know about the mother and then its offspring. From where do I know about the offspring and then its mother?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says 'don't think that' and starts quoting a ברייתא. This step sets up the question, and the next step gives the ברייתא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא agrees that the plain words only cover mother first, then offspring. It then asks openly where the reverse order (offspring first, then mother) is learned from. This shows that the תנאים already dealt with the problem and found a source.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Do not let it enter your mind', a rejection of the assumption just raised
'I only have…', the plain פסוק teaches only this much
From where? (asking for a source in the Torah)

phrases.english: Do not think so, as it is taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: ״אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ״ – אֵין לִי אֶלָּא אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ,
phrases.english: 'It and its offspring': I only have the mother and then its offspring,
from where do I know about the offspring and then its mother?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18 by rejecting it and opening a ברייתא that deals with the same question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the assumption and brings a ברייתא with a source in the תורה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only slaughtering the mother first and then the offspring is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: A ברייתא shows that the reverse order is also included (the source is spelled out in the next step).

steps.title: The plural 'you shall not slaughter' teaches that both orders are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the plural word לא תשחטו that two people can be liable. One person who kills the mother after the offspring, and another who kills the offspring after the mother, are both חייבין.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it says 'you (plural) shall not slaughter', that means two people. How so? One slaughters the cow, another slaughters its mother, and another slaughters its offspring. The last two are liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its source: the plural verb לא תשחטו. It shows a case where two people are punished, one for each order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural shows that the Torah has in mind more than one guilty slaughterer. In the example, after the middle cow is slaughtered, the person who slaughters its mother is guilty (offspring first, then mother), and so is the person who slaughters its offspring (mother first, then offspring). That proves the משנה's ruling: slaughtering the mother after the offspring is also forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You (plural) shall not slaughter', the plural verb in the פסוק
'How so?', introducing an example that explains the point
Liable (here, to lashes)

steps.whatToRemember: The איסור of אותו ואת בנו works in both directions. Mother then offspring, or offspring then mother: both are forbidden on the same day. This is learned from the plural לא תשחטו.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the משנה's lashes in cases where the mother is slaughtered last.

phrases.english: When it says 'you shall not slaughter',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:28. The verb is plural, which is the key to the derivation.

phrases.english: here there are two. How so?
phrases.notes: 'Two' means two different people who can each be guilty.

phrases.english: One person slaughters the cow,
and another slaughters its mother,
and another slaughters its offspring:
the last two are liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר ״לֹא תִשְׁחֲטוּ״ – הֲרֵי כָּאן שְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא by answering its own question from step 19.
steps.raayaObject: That slaughtering the offspring first and then the mother is also forbidden, as the משנה rules.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The plural verb לא תשחטו in ויקרא 22:28, which shows two separate liable slaughterers, one for each order.
